articles.title: The truth about dying: hospice workers on what loved ones should know
articles.description: Anna Gordon met hospice care workers across the UK, learning how dignity and choice help create meaningful moments for patients Most people in the UK actively avoid conversations about death and dying. They can be visibly uncomfortable when you raise the subject. When people try to talk about it, it tends to be euphemistically. This is a mistake, one that can stop you from making important choices for yourself or your loved ones. It can increase fear and misunderstanding about what death can look like, while open conversations can help to ease these feelings and bring a sense of calm, peace and, on occasion, even beauty to the event.
